title: Reinforced Hinge Beam and Intercostal Set for the Fan Cowl Doors

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Stiffens the fan cowl door hinge beam and adds two intercostals at the aft hinge stations, after in-service distortion of the door edge began to make the latch alignment marginal on high-utilisation aircraft.

sections.reason: Line stations reported increasing difficulty closing the fan cowl doors on older aircraft, with the aft latch needing to be pulled into engagement by hand. Measurement of eighteen doors showed a consistent permanent set at the aft hinge station, growing with the number of door opening cycles rather than with flight hours. The door is opened at every transit inspection on some operations, so the cycle count is high. A door that has to be forced closed is a door that can be left unlatched, and the consequence of that is well understood, so the programme treated this as a safety-driven change rather than a handling nuisance.
sections.description: The fan cowl door hinge beam is stiffened by the addition of the spar cap D5410128007885 along its full length and the two intercostals D5410120303178 and D5410127058517 at the aft hinge stations. The gusset D5410123630218 is added at the aft hinge fitting to close the load path into the door skin. Cable ties AES858082K2 are used to restrain the drain line that the new intercostals displace. The latch keeper positions are unchanged, so a modified door and an unmodified door can both be latched to the same nacelle. The door is worked off the aircraft in a jig, and the drilling of the new intercostal positions is done from a template rather than to a datum. Work is in zones 443 and 441 and is detailed on drawings D54101222003 and D54101234616. The thrust reverser structure and the inlet cowl are unaffected.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 8.7 kg per door, giving 34.8 kg per aircraft, applied symmetrically. The centre-of-gravity effect is negligible because the mass is close to the reference station. No electrical effect. Modified and unmodified doors are interchangeable on the aircraft, but the door parts are not interchangeable at detail level and a modified door may not be reverted. Dispatch and the minimum equipment list are unaffected. Structure repair manual content for the door, the removal and installation tasks, and the illustrated parts breakdown all require update.
sections.embodiment_note: Production cut-in at MSN T00175 in August 2020. Retrofit through the associated service bulletin, with the doors removed and worked in a shop; the aircraft can be released with a serviceable exchange pair while its own doors are modified. Two working days per door pair.

type_data.balance_impact: Symmetric, close to reference station, negligible CG effect
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN T00175, no line stoppage
